newsitem.title: USA: Dow tumbles 140 points as blue chips beat retreat.
newsitem.headline: Dow tumbles 140 points as blue chips beat retreat.

text.p: U.S. blue chips turned sharply lower in late afternoon Wednesday as investors began looking beyond the Dow industrials for their next opportunity.

The Dow industrials fell 148 points to 7814 before finding its footing and recovering to 7860, off 102 points for the session. The New York Stock Exchange imposed its second level of program trading limits, the so-called "sidecar" curbs, at 1502 EDT/1902 GMT.
While the Dow was spiraling lower, other market segments were far less affected by the selling pressure. Tech stocks clung to gains and small cap stocks edged only mildly lower.
Bonds were higher, with the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury up 10/32 to yield 6.56 percent.
"It looks like we're seeing some asset allocation shifting trading from stocks into bonds," said Charles Pradilla, market analyst at Cowen and Co. "A lot of big cap stocks got overvalued."
Market breadth turned decidedly negative, with three decliners for every two advancers on heavy NYSE volume of more than 510 million shares.
